### Summary

### Steps to reproduce

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->

1. Create a test group and/or project
2. Create 31 or more issues in the project
3. Retrieve the issues (can be used in a test) and verify that only 30 issues are returned. This is because the api package uses
the default list limit of [30](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/blob/d3e5058b40f75359ed1b12c03e112886688cc281/api/default.go#L3).

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

<!-- What actually happens -->

The api call (and possibly other api calls) only retrieve the first 30 results.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

<!-- What you should see instead -->

The api call should retrieve all results, or allow the calling function to paginate through the available issues.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

<!--- Paste the activity log from your command line -->

### Possible fixes

<!-- If you can, link to the line of code that might be responsible for the problem -->

Refactor the [api.ListIssues](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/blob/d3e5058b40f75359ed1b12c03e112886688cc281/api/issue.go#L92) function so that it
returns a value for iterating through the remaining pages. For example, it could return `([]*gitlab.Issue, bool, err)` where the boolean value is true if there's a next page and false otherwise.

### Summary

<!-- Summarize the bug encountered concisely -->

`glab api graphql` does not support complex variables. For example:

```shell
glab api graphql \
  -f query='mutation($input: UpdateIssueInput!){updateIssue(input: $input){errors issue{id state title}}}' \
```

- GLAB: glab version DEV

<!--

-->

### Steps to reproduce

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->

Attempt to do a graphql mutation with the CLI that requires complex (i.e. a JSON object) variables. For example:

```shell
glab api graphql \
  -f query='mutation($input: UpdateIssueInput!){updateIssue(input: $input){errors issue{id state title}}}' \
  -f input='{"iid":"16", "projectPath":"bmendric/nvim-config", "stateEvent":"CLOSE"}'
```

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

<!-- What actually happens -->

Running the above query results in: 

```json
glab: Variable $input of type UpdateIssueInput! was provided invalid value
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "Variable $input of type UpdateIssueInput! was provided invalid value",
      "locations": [
        {
          "line": 1,
          "column": 10
        }
      ],
      "extensions": {
        "value": "{\"iid\":\"16\", \"projectPath\":\"bmendric/nvim-config\", \"stateEvent\":\"CLOSE\"}",
        "problems": [
          {
            "path": [],
            "explanation": "Expected \"{\\\"iid\\\":\\\"16\\\", \\\"projectPath\\\":\\\"bmendric/nvim-config\\\", \\\"stateEvent\\\":\\\"CLOSE\\\"}\" to be a key-value object."
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

In other words, the variable is being treated as an encoded string rather than being passed directly through. The result is valid, but incorrectly formatted, JSON that GitLab's graphql correctly rejects.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

<!-- What you should see instead -->

glab should have some way to supply more complex data structure to the graphql api request such that the above request is possible.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

<!--- Paste the activity log from your command line -->

N/a

### Possible fixes

<!-- If you can, link to the line of code that might be responsible for the problem -->

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/commands/api/http.go?ref_type=heads#L60 -- There is some parsing that glab is already doing to, apparently, deal with array objects. In theory, it would be possible to write some regex to do similar things to the array handling, however, this feels like the incorrect approach.

Rather, I would expect `--raw-field` parameters to generally be treated as `json.RawMessage` objects so they are passed directly through to the request. Since this is a bit niche, here's an example https://go.dev/play/p/vargAvVKPZV
title: `glab api graphql` does not support complex variable types

This was requested by several people in the feedback issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/7473#note_1954065659

> I wish it could support creating stacks from existing branches in the future: `glab stack infer "My new awesome stack from the working branch"`. That way I don't have to strictly follow the 'stacking process' and just work as usual in one branch. After I've finished the work I can split it using stacks and enjoy the awesome features it brings!

> i could not find references for this use case. however, i can imagine how it can be handy to be able to infer stacked diffs from a branch. the main advantage i see is it will enable authors to apply the paradigm on existing work, allowing them to benefit from it earlier.

> A use case I could see for something like `glab stack infer` would be to allow the team to mostly still use standard git commits in their day-to-day, but use `glab stack` to handle cases were I want to build off (stack off) of someone else's work. It is a slightly different use case, but also quite common on teams for someone to need just the first 1 or 2 of someone's diff.

>>>
This was my first question when attempting to use it. I have an existing branch that I would like to specify as the first diff in a new stack.

This seems like a normal use case. Maybe I don't always want to use stacked diffs, and would prefer to use normal git usually, but only switch to a stack when I actually have multiple branches to rebase on top of each other. However I don't always know in advance when I'm going to need it.
>>>

> This was also my first misstep. Without re-watching the video, I made a commit, and tried `glab stack save` and got `no changes to save`; however, there was a diff in `git log @{u}..HEAD`.

Make it so that stacks can be created from existing commits on the current active branch.

### Summary

The `glab api` command's `-F` flag has array detection logic (`stringArrayRegexPattern` in `internal/commands/api/http.go`) that only matches bracket-enclosed values where each element consists of lowercase letters and underscores (`[[:lower:]_]`). This causes array-type API parameters to be sent as strings when values contain hyphens, uppercase letters, digits, or other common characters.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Attempt to set project topics
glab api -X PUT projects/:id -F "topics=[my-topic, GitLab]"
# Expected: {"topics":["my-topic","GitLab"]}
# Actual:   {"topics":"[my-topic, GitLab]"} (string, not array)

# Even single values fail with -f
glab api -X PUT projects/:id -f "topics=nomograph"
# Expected: {"topics":["nomograph"]}
# Actual:   {"topics":"nomograph"} (string, not array)
```

### What is the current bug behavior?

The `stringArrayRegexPattern` regex (`^\[\s*([[:lower:]_]+(\s*,\s*[[:lower:]_]+)*)?\s*\]$`) rejects:
- Hyphens (`my-topic`)
- Uppercase (`GitLab`)
- Digits (`topic2`)
- Quoted strings (`"my topic"`)

Values that don't match the regex are serialized as JSON strings instead of arrays.

### What is the expected correct behavior?

Array parameters should be correctly serialized to JSON arrays for any valid string values, not just `[a-z_]` tokens.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

The existing test case in `http_test.go` only covers the happy path:
```go
params: map[string]any{"scopes": "[api, read_api]"},
want: expects{body: `{"scopes":["api","read_api"]}`},
```

No test cases exist for values containing hyphens, uppercase, digits, quoted strings, or empty arrays.

### Environment

Affects all versions with the current regex. Verified against `main` branch source.

### Possible fixes

**Option A (minimal):** Broaden the regex character class to accept common characters in API values.

**Option B (robust):** If a `-F` value is valid JSON (starts with `[` or `{`), parse with `json.Unmarshal` and use the parsed value directly. This would also fix #7467 (complex GraphQL variables).

### Proposed test coverage

The following cases should be added to `Test_httpRequest` in `http_test.go` to prevent regression and validate the fix:

```go
{
    name: "POST with hyphenated array elements",
    args: args{
        host:   "gitlab.com",
        method: http.MethodPost,
        p:      "projects",
        params: map[string]any{"topics": "[my-topic, knowledge-graph]"},
        headers: []string{},
    },
    want: expects{
        method: http.MethodPost,
        u:      "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects",
        body:   `{"topics":["my-topic","knowledge-graph"]}`,
    },
},
{
    name: "POST with uppercase array elements",
    args: args{
        host:   "gitlab.com",
        method: http.MethodPost,
        p:      "projects",
        params: map[string]any{"topics": "[GitLab, CI]"},
        headers: []string{},
    },
    want: expects{
        method: http.MethodPost,
        u:      "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects",
        body:   `{"topics":["GitLab","CI"]}`,
    },
},
{
    name: "POST with digits in array elements",
    args: args{
        host:   "gitlab.com",
        method: http.MethodPost,
        p:      "projects",
        params: map[string]any{"topics": "[topic1, v2]"},
        headers: []string{},
    },
    want: expects{
        method: http.MethodPost,
        u:      "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects",
        body:   `{"topics":["topic1","v2"]}`,
    },
},
{
    name: "POST with single array element",
    args: args{
        host:   "gitlab.com",
        method: http.MethodPost,
        p:      "projects",
        params: map[string]any{"topics": "[nomograph]"},
        headers: []string{},

    want: expects{
```

## Problem

There is no single command to connect an AI coding agent to Orbit. Today a user needs to:
1. Find and read the MCP setup docs
2. Manually write the MCP config for their specific agent
3. Separately find, clone, and symlink the orbit skill into their agent's skills directory

This is three steps across two different concepts (MCP + skills) with agent-specific instructions for each. It breaks down entirely for agents without documented skill conventions.

## Proposal

`glab orbit setup` - one command that gives any AI coding agent full Orbit capability.

```
$ glab orbit setup

✓ Detected Claude Code (~/.claude/)
✓ MCP server registered: gitlab-orbit → https://gitlab.com/api/v4/orbit/mcp
✓ Skill installed: ~/.claude/skills/orbit/

Orbit is ready. Ask your agent: "Check the Orbit API status"
```

## What it does

**1. Writes the MCP config** for the detected agent

Registers the Orbit MCP endpoint (`https://gitlab.com/api/v4/orbit/mcp`) in the agent's MCP config. Format varies by agent:

| Agent | Config target |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/settings.json` (mcpServers) |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.json` (mcpServers) |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/settings.json` (mcpServers) |
| Unknown | Prints the JSON snippet to stdout for manual paste |

**2. Installs the orbit skill** for agents that support skills

Downloads the orbit skill from `gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph` (or reads from the embedded binary once bundled via `glab skills`) and writes it to the agent's skills directory.

| Agent | Skill target |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/orbit/` |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/skills/orbit/` |
| Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI | No skill convention yet - MCP only |

**3. Verifies the connection**

Calls `glab api orbit/status` and reports whether the service is reachable. If the `knowledge_graph` feature flag is off, surfaces a clear error with the chatops command to enable it.

## Flags

```
--agent <name>     Override auto-detection (claude-code, cursor, opencode)
--mcp-only         Skip skill installation
--skill-only       Skip MCP config
--dry-run          Print what would be done without writing anything
```

## Agent detection

Auto-detect by checking for known config directories in order:
- Claude Code: `~/.claude/` exists
- Cursor: `~/.cursor/` exists
- OpenCode: `~/.config/opencode/` exists
- Fallback: print universal MCP JSON to stdout

## Why glab owns this

- glab already holds the user's GitLab auth (no extra token setup)
- glab knows the instance URL (no hardcoded gitlab.com)
- works for both .com and self-managed once Orbit ships there

## Related

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/591015 - Integrate Orbit into glab CLI
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8252 - `glab skills` command
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8240 - `glab orbit` POC
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/work_items/387 - MCP setup docs
- https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/20357 - GKG Core Development Workstream
title: glab orbit setup - one command to install Orbit MCP config + skill for any AI coding agent

## Summary

The Orbit local CLI now publishes Windows binaries starting with [v0.59.1](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/releases/v0.59.1). The `glab orbit local` command currently rejects Windows up front (`SupportedOS` is `["darwin", "linux"]`) and the platform-specific executor returns "Orbit local CLI is not supported on Windows".

We can now lift that restriction and let Windows users run `glab orbit local` end-to-end.

## What changed upstream

Release `v0.59.1` adds the following assets to the generic package registry:

- `orbit-local-windows-x86_64.zip` (single `orbit.exe` at archive root)
- `orbit-local-windows-x86_64.zip.sha256`

Only `x86_64` is published. ARM64 Windows transparently runs x64 binaries under emulation on Windows 11, so we can route ARM64 to the same asset.

## Scope of glab changes

| Area | Today | Needed |
|---|---|---|
| `SupportedOS` (orbit local Spec) | `darwin`, `linux` | add `windows` |
| Arch normalization | rejects Windows | return `x86_64` for any Windows GOARCH |
| Asset name | always `.tar.gz` | `.zip` on Windows |
| Installed binary name | always `orbit` | `orbit.exe` on Windows |
| Archive extractor | `TarGzExtractor` only | add `ZipExtractor` and pick by archive extension |
| `executeOrbit` on Windows | stub returning error | subprocess execution (mirroring Duo CLI Windows path) |
| Error handling | n/a | wrap `ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT` with a hint about x64 emulation on ARM64 |

The binary manager (`internal/binarymgr`) already supports Windows in its install path; the work is concentrated in the orbit local command and a new shared zip extractor.

## Out of scope

- Native ARM64 Windows binary (waiting on upstream).
- Removing the experimental flag — Windows starts as best-effort.

## Acceptance criteria

- `glab orbit local --install` succeeds on Windows x64 and ARM64 (Windows 11).
- Downloaded archive is checksum-verified, extracted to the managed bin directory, and invoked via subprocess.
- Clear error message when running on ARM64 Windows without x64 emulation.
- Unit tests cover the zip extractor, Windows arch normalization, asset naming, and the error-wrapping path.

## Related

- Upstream release: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/orbit/knowledge-graph/-/releases/v0.59.1
- Existing precedent for Windows-supported managed binaries: `glab duo cli`

## Problem

`make gen-docs` (`cmd/gen-docs/docs.go`) writes a Markdown page for every available command, but it **never deletes** pages for commands that later become unavailable — hidden, deprecated, or removed. The stale `.md` lingers under `docs/source/`.

Concrete example: `glab duo ask` is `Hidden: true` + `Deprecated`, so `gen-docs` correctly skips *generating* it — yet `docs/source/duo/ask.md` still exists on disk from before those flags were set. The page stays published and reachable by URL even though nothing links to it.

This surfaced while making the GitLab Docs `glab` navigation generated rather than hand-maintained (see gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com#671 and gitlab-org/technical-writing/docs-gitlab-com#669). Once the nav is derived from the command tree, dropping an unavailable command from the nav leaves its still-present source page orphaned.

## Proposed fix — marker-based pruning

Every generated page already carries a marker comment:

```
<!--
This documentation is auto generated by a script.
Please do not edit this file directly. Run `make gen-docs` instead.
-->
```

`gen-docs` can prune safely by keying off that marker:

1. Build the set of expected output paths from the command tree (the generator already walks it).
2. Walk `docs/source/` and delete any file that **contains the generated-by-a-script marker** and is **not** in the expected set.

The marker check is what makes this safe: hand-maintained content (e.g. `img/`, the custom root `_index.md` intro, `changelog`) has no marker and is never touched. This handles renames and removals, not just the `duo ask` case.

## Wire into the drift check

`lefthook.yml` already regenerates docs and fails on drift (`check-docs` pre-commit, `check-generated` pre-push). With pruning in place, a `git diff docs/` after `make gen-docs` would also catch a stale page that should have been deleted — so removals stay enforced the same way out-of-date pages are today.

## Acceptance

- Running `make gen-docs` after hiding/deprecating/removing a command deletes its generated page(s).
- Hand-maintained, non-generated files under `docs/source/` are untouched.
- The existing drift checks fail if a stale generated page remains.
- As a first beneficiary, `docs/source/duo/ask.md` is removed.
title: gen-docs: prune generated pages for unavailable (hidden/deprecated/removed) commands

## Background

Cobra/pflag flag-deprecation warnings (`Flag --x has been deprecated, ...`) are written to **stdout** in `glab`, not stderr. pflag's own default is stderr, but cobra buffers the message and flushes it via `c.Print(...)` (`command.go:1885`), which resolves to `OutOrStderr()` and walks the parent chain to glab's root command, where `root.go:128` does `rootCmd.SetOut(f.IO().StdOut)`. So every child command inherits stdout as the deprecation-warning sink.

This is reproducible on `main` with any deprecated flag, for example:

```
$ glab variable export --format json 1>out.txt 2>err.txt
# out.txt contains: Flag --format has been deprecated, use --output instead.
```

The practical problem is for commands whose stdout is structured data meant for piping. A user mid-migration who runs e.g. `glab orbit remote query --response-format raw` via the deprecated `--format raw` and pipes into `jq` gets the warning prepended to the JSON stream, so `jq` fails to parse. Warnings should not pollute the data channel.

## Proposal

Route flag-deprecation warnings to stderr - either by adjusting the root command wiring so deprecation output goes to `f.IO().StdErr`, or by an upstream cobra change. We should keep stdout reserved for command data.

### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (`glab --version`): **1.102.0**
- [x] Operating System and version: Linux (Fedora 38)

### Summary

When two accounts are configured for the **same** GitLab instance — the primary under the real host key, and a second account under a *synthetic* host key whose `api_host` points back at the real host — repo-scoped commands (`glab ci list`, `glab mr list`, `glab issue list`, …) cannot auto-detect the second account for a repository whose remote uses an **SSH host alias**. glab always resolves to the primary account.

The identical setup works correctly when the remote is **HTTPS**, because the URL host is matched against the configured host keys literally. Only the SSH path is affected.

### Setup

`~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml`:

```yaml
hosts:
  gitlab.com:            # primary account
    token: <token-A>
    user: alice
  gitlab.com-work:       # second account, same instance
    api_host: gitlab.com
    token: <token-B>
    user: alice-work
    ssh_host: gitlab.com
```

`~/.ssh/config` (the alias is required so `git` push/pull can use a different key for the second account):

```
Host gitlab.com-work
  HostName gitlab.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_work
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone a project that only the **second** account can see, via the SSH alias:
   `git clone git@gitlab.com-work:group/private-repo.git`
2. Inside the clone, run any repo-scoped command, e.g. `glab ci list` or `glab mr list`.

### Current behaviour

glab authenticates as the **primary** account (`gitlab.com` / `token-A`) and returns `404 Project Not Found`, because that account cannot see the second account's private project.

Setting `GITLAB_HOST=gitlab.com-work` (or passing `--hostname gitlab.com-work`) is a working workaround, but pure auto-detection from the remote resolves to the wrong account.

### Expected behaviour

For a remote whose SSH host is `gitlab.com-work`, glab should resolve to the `gitlab.com-work` config entry (`token-B`) — the same way it already does for an HTTPS remote `https://gitlab.com-work/...`.

### Root cause

In `internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go`, the remote URL is passed through the SSH-config translator (`git.ParseSSHConfig().Translator()`) **before** account matching. For the SSH alias `gitlab.com-work`, the translator applies the `HostName gitlab.com` line from `~/.ssh/config` and rewrites the host to `gitlab.com`. Matching then happens on `gitlab.com`, which is a known host bound to the primary account, so the second entry is never reached.

The `sshHostMapping` built from the entries' `ssh_host` values is only consulted when the resolved host is **not** in `knownHosts`. After translation the host is `gitlab.com`, which is always known, so in the auto-detect path the mapping never applies.

HTTPS remotes are unaffected because the translator only rewrites `ssh://` URLs (the scheme switch in the resolver, and `internal/git` `ParseURL`), so the literal host `gitlab.com-work` survives and matches the config key.

### Proposed fix

Match the remote's **literal** (pre-translation) SSH host against the configured host keys (and each entry's `ssh_host`) **first**, and only fall back to SSH-config translation when no configured entry matches the literal host. This makes the SSH path consistent with the HTTPS path: `git@gitlab.com-work:...` would resolve to the `gitlab.com-work` entry directly, without depending on the `HostName` value in `~/.ssh/config`.

### Offer

I'm happy to open an MR implementing this if the approach sounds reasonable — please let me know your preference on where the literal-host check should sit (in the resolver before `sshTranslate`, or inside `TranslateRemotes`).
title: Remote resolver picks the wrong account for two accounts on one instance when the remote uses an SSH alias

Environment: glab 1.108.0 (Homebrew, macOS arm64), gitlab.com, logged in via `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com --web --use-keyring`

Steps to reproduce:
1. `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com --web --use-keyring` (config ends up with is_oauth2: "true", use_keyring: "true")
2. Wait for the OAuth access token to expire (~2 h), or just run:
3. `printf "protocol=https\nhost=gitlab.com\n" | glab auth git-credential get`

Actual: 
```
ERROR Expected OAuthTokenSource auth source for "gitlab.com", got api.oauth2AccessTokenOnlyAuthSource.
```
Every git fetch/push/pull over HTTPS fails, while `glab auth status` reports everything green (it never exercises this code path). `oauth2_expiry_date` in config.yml is never updated.
```
grep oauth2_expiry_date "$HOME/Library/Application Support/glab-cli/config.yml"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
glab auth status
grep oauth2_expiry_date "$HOME/Library/Application Support/glab-cli/config.yml"

        oauth2_expiry_date: "2026-07-20T14:48:34+02:00"
gitlab.com
  ✓ Logged in to gitlab.com as xxx (keyring)
  ✓ Git operations for gitlab.com configured to use https protocol.
  ✓ API calls for gitlab.com are made over https protocol.
  ✓ REST API Endpoint: https://gitlab.com/api/v4/
  ✓ GraphQL Endpoint: https://gitlab.com/api/graphql/
  ✓ Token found: **************************
        oauth2_expiry_date: "2026-07-20T14:48:34+02:00"
```

Expected: the credential helper refreshes (or at least forwards) the token, as it did before 1.108.0.

Suspicion: interaction between the git-credential refresh logic (!2485) and 1.108.0's fix(auth): preserve saved values on re-authentication. With `--use_keyring` the auth source is constructed as access-token-only, failing the OAuthTokenSource type assertion.

Workaround: re-login without `--use-keyring.`
